```{r}
head(daily_summary, 5)
```

```{r}
start_date <- min(daily_summary$day)
```

```{r}
# create proportions
daily_summary <- daily_summary %>%
  mutate(
    prop_news = (count_ng_domains / tweet_count) * 100,
    prop_misinfo = ((count_caution + count_max_caution) / tweet_count) * 100,
    prop_anger = (count_anger_065 / n_scored) * 100,
    prop_fear = (count_fear_065 / n_scored) * 100,

```




## Univariate ARIMA models and outlier detection

First, we run univariate ARIMA models with an automated method that automatically fits an ARIMA model (auto.arima from the forecast package).


### Tweet count

```{r}
# extract dates
start_date <- min(daily_summary$day)
start_year <- year(start_date)
start_day  <- yday(start_date)

# convert to time series object
ts_count <- ts(daily_summary$tweet_count, 
               start = c(start_year, start_day), 
               frequency = 7 #--> use 7 to induce weekly seasonality 
               )

# fit the model without any specifications
arima_count <- auto.arima(ts_count, seasonal = TRUE)
summary(arima_count)
```

* There is a first-order differencing to remove a stochastic trend (d=1)
* Daily volatility with corrections (AR/MA terms)
* Weekly seasonality, probably weekday vs weekend
* High absolute variability/day-to-day swings



```{r}
checkresiduals(arima_count)
```

Ljung-Box: there is still significant autocorrelation. The ACF plot shows the autocorrelation of residuals at different lags (=how each residual is correlated with previous residuals: lag 1 with lag 2, etc.). All bars should fall within the blue dotted lines (95% confidence interval). There are some spikes at lag 14 and lag 28 that exceed the 95%CI but there does not seem to be an obvious temporal pattern/structure. 

The residuals fluctuate across the whole time period and there are some positive and negative spikes early and late in the series, suggesting outliers, events, or structural changes.
*--> check outliers!*

Now we're testing for outliers / abrupt changes in the time series with with tso() from tsoutliers, which gives us the type of outliers (compared to tsoutliers() from forecast)

```{r}
count_outliers <- tso(ts_count, 
                      types = c("AO", "LS", "TC"), # all types
                      tsmethod = "arima",
                      cval=3.75,
                      args.tsmethod = list(order = c(3,1,5), 
                                           seasonal = list(order = c(2, 0, 0), 
                                                           period = 7))
                      ) 

summary(count_outliers)
```

There are 21 outliers, let's look at them and transform the lags into dates:

```{r}
# write function to add the date based on the date index
add_outlier_dates <- function(outlier_df, start_date) {
  outlier_df %>%
    mutate(day = as.Date(start_date) + (ind - 1))
}

count_df <- count_outliers$outliers
count_df <- add_outlier_dates(count_df, start_date)
print(count_df)
```


```{r}
plot(count_outliers)
```

We can see that the tweet count has consistently gone up at two different points in time (the level shifts) and on a bunch of individual days.


### News count 

```{r}
ts_domains <- ts(daily_summary$prop_news, 
               start = c(start_year, start_day), 
               frequency = 7)

arima_domains <- auto.arima(ts_domains, seasonal=TRUE)
summary(arima_domains)
```

Overall, there's no differencing, the data is already stationary in its level (no integration). It follows strong 2-day cycles (AR2=0.82). 

There are two SAR terms suggesting a strong weekly pattern, so what happens today is similar to what happened 1 and 2 weeks ago.

So this could reflect bursty news cycles — e.g., certain news domains go viral mid-week and fade, with clear weekly rhythms in how news is shared.

```{r}
checkresiduals(arima_domains)
```

```{r}
fdGPH(residuals(arima_domains))
```
Running some integration tests

```{r}
adf_test <- ur.df(ts_domains, type = "trend")
kpss_test <- ur.kpss(ts_domains, type = "tau")

summary(adf_test)   # H0: unit root (series is I(1))
summary(kpss_test)  # H0: stationary (series is I(0))
```


```{r}
# also test on deseasonalized data
decomp <- stl(ts_domains, s.window = "periodic")
deseasonalized <- ts_domains - decomp$time.series[, "seasonal"]

adf_deseas <- ur.df(deseasonalized, type = "trend")
kpss_deseas <- ur.kpss(deseasonalized, type = "tau")
summary(adf_deseas)
summary(kpss_deseas)
```

ADF test indicates the series is stationary, whereas the KPSS test says its non-stationary. 
Test fractional integration with ``fracdiff'':

```{r}
d_estimate <- fracdiff(deseasonalized, nar = 0, nma = 0)$d
cat("Fractional integration parameter d =", d_estimate, "\n")
```


```{r}
adf_diff <- ur.df(diff(ts_domains), type = "drift")
summary(adf_diff)
```


```{r}
domain_outliers <- tso(ts_domains,
                      types = c("AO", "LS", "TC"),
                      tsmethod = "arima",
                      cval=3.75, # lower to detect COVID spike 
                      )

domains_df <- domain_outliers$outliers
domains_df <- add_outlier_dates(domains_df, start_date)
print(domains_df)
```

Nine outliers, including some temporary changes

```{r}
plot(domain_outliers)
```

* 2019-05-17: temporary change --> Ibiza-Skandal
* 2021-10-06: temporary change --> Inseratenaffäre
* 2021-11-16: temporary change --> mandatory vaccination campaign is announced

### Fraction of untrustworthy tweets

```{r}
ts_score <- ts(daily_summary$prop_misinfo, 
               start = c(start_year, start_day), 
               frequency = 7)

arima_score <- auto.arima(ts_score, seasonal = TRUE)
summary(arima_score)
```

```{r}
checkresiduals(arima_score)
```

Model quality is not so good, its hardest to predict. 


*--> check for level shifts / more permanent changes*


```{r}
score_outliers <- tso(ts_score, # wouldnt converge so had to add some specifications
                      types = c("AO", "LS", "TC"),
                      tsmethod = "arima",
                      args.tsmethod = list(order = c(0,1,2),
                                           seasonal = list(order = c(2,0,0),
                                                           period = 7))
                      )

score_df <- score_outliers$outliers
score_df <- add_outlier_dates(score_df, start_date)
print(score_df)
```

Found 6 outliers!
Including a level shifts and some temporary changes! Let's have a look:

```{r}
plot(score_outliers)
```



#### Intervention analysis

So now, we want to understand the effect of the intervention and we have to create a dummy variable for this. 

```{r}
score_intervention_index <- 1278
n_obs <- length(ts_score)

step <- ifelse(seq_len(n_obs) >= score_intervention_index, 1, 0)

ramp <- c(rep(0, score_intervention_index - 1), 
          seq(1, n_obs - score_intervention_index + 1))

xreg <- cbind(step = step, ramp = ramp)

# rerun model with dummy variable
score_intervention <- auto.arima(ts_score, 
                                 seasonal = TRUE,
                                 xreg = xreg,
                                 stepwise = FALSE) 
summary(score_intervention)
```

*step* = average value of ts_score dropped by 2.9 points 
*ramp* = after that drop, it began increasing by ~0.0002 per day

```{r}
score_intervention_index2 <- 1336
step1 <- ifelse(seq_len(n_obs) >= score_intervention_index, 1, 0)  
step2 <- ifelse(seq_len(n_obs) >= score_intervention_index2, 1, 0)  # second level shift 
xreg2 <- cbind(step1 = step1, step2 = step2)
score_2interventions <- auto.arima(ts_score, seasonal=TRUE, xreg=xreg2, stepwise=FALSE)
summary(score_2interventions)
```

```{r}
# create time series for pre-intervention
ts_score_pre <- ts(ts_score[1:(score_intervention_index - 1)],
                   frequency = frequency(ts_score),
                   start = start(ts_score))

model_cf <- auto.arima(ts_score_pre)



# forecast post-intervention period
h <- length(ts_score) - score_intervention_index + 1
fc <- forecast(model_cf, h = h)
start_fc <- time(ts_score)[score_intervention_index]
fc_ts <- ts(as.numeric(fc$mean),
            start = start_fc,
            frequency = frequency(ts_score))


# plot everything together
fitted_vals <- fitted(score_intervention)

pdf(file.path(dst, "figures/score_intervention.pdf"), width=9, height=4.5)
plot(ts_score, 
     col = "black", 
     lwd = 1, 
     ylab = "Score", 
     xlab = "Time")

lines(fitted_vals, 
      col = "blue", 
      lwd = 2)

lines(fc_ts, 
      col = "red", 
      lwd = 2, 
      lty = "dashed")

abline(v = time(ts_score)[score_intervention_index], 
       col = "red", lty = "dashed")
abline(v = time(ts_score)[score_intervention_index2],  # add this
       col = "red", lty = "dashed", lwd = 1.5)

# legend
legend("topleft",
       legend = c("Observed", "Fitted", "Counterfactual"),
       col = c("black", "blue", "red"),
       lty = c(1, 1, 2),
       lwd = 2)

dev.off()
```


```{r}
cumulative_effect <- coef(score_2interventions)["step1"] + 
                     coef(score_2interventions)["step2"]
print(cumulative_effect); mean(ts_score_pre)
```


### Anger

```{r}
ts_anger <- ts(daily_summary$prop_anger, 
               start = c(start_year, start_day), 
               frequency = 7)

arima_anger <- auto.arima(ts_anger, seasonal=TRUE)
summary(arima_anger)
```


```{r}
checkresiduals(arima_anger)
```

Residual diagnostics show some outliers but overall the model fits well/has predictable patterns


```{r}
# ARIMA orders for tso() taken from the auto.arima fit (previously hard-coded)
tso_args <- function(fit) {
  o <- arimaorder(fit)
  seas <- if (length(o) >= 6) o[4:6] else c(0, 0, 0)
  list(order = unname(o[1:3]), seasonal = list(order = unname(seas), period = 7))
}

# with tso() from tsoutliers
anger_outliers <- tso(ts_anger, 
                      types = c("AO", "LS", "TC"),
                      tsmethod = "arima",
                      args.tsmethod = tso_args(arima_anger)
                      )

anger_df <- anger_outliers$outliers
anger_df <- add_outlier_dates(anger_df, start_date)
print(anger_df)
```

Found a lot of TC outliers but no level shifts.

### Fear

```{r}
# convert to time series object
ts_fear <- ts(daily_summary$prop_fear, 
               start = c(start_year, start_day), 
               frequency = 7)

arima_fear <- auto.arima(ts_fear, seasonal=TRUE)
summary(arima_fear)
```

* fear levels are mostly influenced by what happened yesterday: its sticky  and sustains high
* strong immediate reversal at MA(1), then gradually returns
* doesn't have weekly rhythms like anger 

```{r}
checkresiduals(arima_fear)
```

Residuals are centered around zero with stable variance and two peaks. ACF plot shows that spikes are mostly within the confidence interval. The histogram shows a tail.


```{r}
fear_outliers <- tso(ts_fear, 
                     types = c("AO", "LS", "TC"),
                     tsmethod = "arima",
                     args.tsmethod = tso_args(arima_fear)
                     ) 

fear_df <- fear_outliers$outliers
fear_df <- add_outlier_dates(fear_df, start_date)
print(fear_df)
```

There's a level shift at index 660 (first submission: all languages, Q3; check for the revised series).

### Disgust

```{r, eval = DISGUST}
ts_disgust <- ts(daily_summary$prop_disgust,
                 start = c(start_year, start_day),
                 frequency = 7)

arima_disgust <- auto.arima(ts_disgust, seasonal = TRUE)
summary(arima_disgust)
checkresiduals(arima_disgust)
```

```{r, eval = DISGUST}
disgust_outliers <- tso(ts_disgust,
                        types = c("AO", "LS", "TC"),
                        tsmethod = "arima",
                        args.tsmethod = tso_args(arima_disgust))

disgust_df <- add_outlier_dates(disgust_outliers$outliers, start_date)
print(disgust_df)
```


Explanation of types: 
AO = additive outlier; one-day peak without any lasting effects
LS = level shift; a permanent change in the time series
TC = temporary change; a sudden change with short-term effects 


## Save tables
```{r}
create_arima_table <- function(arima_model,variable_name) {
  coefs <- coef(arima_model)
  ci_matrix <- confint(arima_model)
  
  aic <- AIC(arima_model)
  bic <- BIC(arima_model)
  loglik <- arima_model$loglik
  
  coef_rows <- data.frame(
    Parameter = names(coefs),
    Coefficient = coefs,
    CI = paste0("[", round(ci_matrix[, 1], 3), ", ", round(ci_matrix[, 2], 3), "]"),
    Value = NA,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
    row.names=NULL
  )
  
  stat_rows <- data.frame(
    Parameter = c("LogLik", "AIC", "BIC"),
    Coefficient = NA,
    CI = NA,
    Value = c(loglik, aic, bic),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  complete_table <- rbind(coef_rows, stat_rows)
  colnames(complete_table)[3] <- "95% CI"
  
  latex_table <- complete_table %>%
    kable(format = "latex",
          booktabs=TRUE,
          linesep = "",
          digits=3)
  
  out <- file.path(dst, paste0("tables/arima_", variable_name, ".tex"))
  writeLines(as.character(latex_table), out)
  
  return(complete_table)
}

count_table <- create_arima_table(arima_count, "count")
count_table
```


```{r}

ci_matrix <- confint(score_2interventions)
```

## Hashtag analysis of outliers (restricted data)

NOTE: This section needs `Austria-Panel-Daily-Hashtags.csv` (daily hashtag lists from
`1c-pull_hashtags.py`). The file contains tweet content and is **not part of the public data
release**, so this section is skipped when the file is missing. It produces `tables/outliers.tex`
(top hashtags on the tweet-count outlier days found above).

```{r}
HAS_HASHTAGS <- file.exists(file.path(src, "Austria-Panel-Daily-Hashtags.csv"))
if (!HAS_HASHTAGS) message("Austria-Panel-Daily-Hashtags.csv not found (not released): skipping the hashtag outlier table.")
```

```{r, eval = HAS_HASHTAGS}
hashtags_df <- read.csv(file.path(src, "Austria-Panel-Daily-Hashtags.csv"))
```

```{r, eval = HAS_HASHTAGS}
top_3_per_day <- hashtags_df %>%
  mutate(hashtag_list = str_split(hashtags, ",")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    top_3 = list(
      hashtag_list %>%
        table() %>%
        sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>%
        names() %>%
        head(3)
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(top_3 = map(top_3, ~ if(length(.x) < 3) c(.x, rep(NA, 3 - length(.x))) 
                              else .x)) %>%
  unnest_wider(top_3, names_sep = "_") %>%
  rename(top_1 = top_3_1, top_2 = top_3_2, top_3 = top_3_3)

```

```{r, eval = HAS_HASHTAGS}
top_3_per_day$day <- as.Date(top_3_per_day$day)
count_df <- left_join(
                      count_df,
                      top_3_per_day, by="day")%>%
  filter(!format(day, "%m-%d") %in% c("12-24", "12-31"))%>%
  mutate(hashtags = paste(top_1, top_2, top_3, sep = ",")) %>%
  dplyr:::select(-top_1, -top_2, -top_3)
count_df
```

```{r, eval = HAS_HASHTAGS}
latex_table <- count_df%>%
    dplyr:::select(day,type, coefhat, tstat, hashtags)%>%
    mutate(hashtags = gsub("مهسا_امینی", "MahsaAmini", hashtags, fixed = TRUE)) %>%
    kable(format = "latex",
          booktabs=TRUE,
          linesep = "")
  
out <- file.path(dst, "tables/outliers.tex")
writeLines(as.character(latex_table), out)
```
